1.zh: 神既在古时借着众先知多次多方地晓谕列祖，
1.en: God, having in the past spoken to the fathers through the prophets at many times and in various ways,

1.zh: 就在这末世借着他儿子晓谕我们；又早已立他为承受万有的，也曾借着他创造诸世界。
1.en: has at the end of these days spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the worlds.

1.zh: 他是　神荣耀所发的光辉，是　神本体的真像，常用他权能的命令托住万有。他洗净了人的罪，就坐在高天至大者的右边。
1.en: His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, who, when he had by himself purified us of our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high,

1.zh: 他所承受的名，既比天使的名更尊贵，就远超过天使。
1.en: having become as much better than the angels as the more excellent name he has inherited is better than theirs.

1.zh: 所有的天使，　神从来对哪一个说： 你是我的儿子， 我今日生你？ 又指着哪一个说： 我要作他的父， 他要作我的子？
1.en: For to which of the angels did he say at any time, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father?” and again, “I will be to him a Father, and he will be to me a Son?”

1.zh: 再者，　神使长子到世上来的时候，就说： 　神的使者都要拜他。
1.en: When he again brings in the firstborn into the world he says, “Let all the angels of God worship him.”

1.zh: 论到使者，又说： 　神以风为使者， 以火焰为仆役；
1.en: Of the angels he says, “He makes his angels winds, and his servants a flame of fire.”

1.zh: 论到子却说： 　神啊，你的宝座是永永远远的； 你的国权是正直的。
1.en: But of the Son he says, “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever. The scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your Kingdom.

1.zh: 你喜爱公义，恨恶罪恶； 所以　神，就是你的　神，用喜乐油膏你， 胜过膏你的同伴；
1.en: You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows.”

1.zh: 又说：主啊，你起初立了地的根基； 天也是你手所造的。
1.en: And, “You, Lord, in the beginning, laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the works of your hands.

1.zh: 天地都要灭没，你却要长存。 天地都要像衣服渐渐旧了；
1.en: They will perish, but you continue. They all will grow old like a garment does.

1.zh: 你要将天地卷起来，像一件外衣， 天地就都改变了。 惟有你永不改变； 你的年数没有穷尽。
1.en: You will roll them up like a mantle, and they will be changed; but you are the same. Your years won’t fail.”

1.zh: 所有的天使，　神从来对哪一个说： 你坐在我的右边， 等我使你仇敌作你的脚凳？
1.en: But which of the angels has he told at any time, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet?”

1.zh: 天使岂不都是服役的灵、奉差遣为那将要承受救恩的人效力吗？
1.en: Aren’t they all serving spirits, sent out to do service for the sake of those who will inherit salvation?

2.zh: 所以，我们当越发郑重所听见的道理，恐怕我们随流失去。
2.en: Therefore we ought to pay greater attention to the things that were heard, lest perhaps we drift away.

2.zh: 那借着天使所传的话既是确定的；凡干犯悖逆的都受了该受的报应。
2.en: For if the word spoken through angels proved steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just penalty,

2.zh: 我们若忽略这么大的救恩，怎能逃罪呢？这救恩起先是主亲自讲的，后来是听见的人给我们证实了。
2.en: how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation—which at the first having been spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard,

2.zh: 神又按自己的旨意，用神迹、奇事和百般的异能，并圣灵的恩赐，同他们作见证。
2.en: God also testifying with them, both by signs and wonders, by various works of power, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will?

2.zh: 我们所说将来的世界，　神原没有交给天使管辖。
2.en: For he didn’t subject the world to come, of which we speak, to angels.

2.zh: 但有人在[经上]某处证明说： 人算什么，你竟顾念他？ 世人算什么，你竟眷顾他？
2.en: But one has somewhere testified, saying, “What is man, that you think of him? Or the son of man, that you care for him?

2.zh: 你叫他比天使微小一点， 赐他荣耀尊贵为冠冕， 并将你手所造的都派他管理，
2.en: You made him a little lower than the angels. You crowned him with glory and honor.

2.zh: 叫万物都服在他的脚下。 既叫万物都服他，就没有剩下一样不服他的。只是如今我们还不见万物都服他。
2.en: You have put all things in subjection under his feet.” For in that he subjected all things to him, he left nothing that is not subject to him. But now we don’t yet see all things subjected to him.

2.zh: 惟独见那成为比天使小一点的耶稣；因为受死的苦，就得了尊贵荣耀为冠冕，叫他因着　神的恩，为人人尝了死味。
2.en: But we see him who has been made a little lower than the angels, Jesus, because of the suffering of death crowned with glory and honor, that by the grace of God he should taste of death for everyone.

2.zh: 原来那为万物所属、为万物所本的，要领许多的儿子进荣耀里去，使救他们的元帅，因受苦难得以完全，本是合宜的。
2.en: For it became him, for whom are all things and through whom are all things, in bringing many children to glory, to make the author of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

2.zh: 因那使人成圣的和那些得以成圣的，都是出于一。所以，他称他们为弟兄也不以为耻，
2.en: For both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one, for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brothers,

2.zh: 说： 我要将你的名传与我的弟兄， 在会中我要颂扬你；
2.en: saying, “I will declare your name to my brothers. Among the congregation I will sing your praise.”

2.zh: 又说： 我要倚赖他； 又说： 看哪，我与　神所给我的儿女。
2.en: Again, “I will put my trust in him.” Again, “Behold, here I am with the children whom God has given me.”

2.zh: 儿女既同有血肉之体，他也照样亲自成了血肉之体，特要借着死败坏那掌死权的，就是魔鬼，
2.en: Since then the children have shared in flesh and blood, he also himself in the same way partook of the same, that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,

2.zh: 并要释放那些一生因怕死而为奴仆的人。
2.en: and might deliver all of them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.

2.zh: 他并不救拔天使，乃是救拔亚伯拉罕的后裔。
2.en: For most certainly, he doesn’t give help to angels, but he gives help to the offspring of Abraham.

2.zh: 所以，他凡事该与他的弟兄相同，为要在　神的事上成为慈悲忠信的大祭司，为百姓的罪献上挽回祭。
2.en: Therefore he was obligated in all things to be made like his brothers, that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.

2.zh: 他自己既然被试探而受苦，就能搭救被试探的人。
2.en: For in that he himself has suffered being tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.

3.zh: 同蒙天召的圣洁弟兄啊，你们应当思想我们所认为使者、为大祭司的耶稣。
3.en: Therefore, holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession: Jesus,

3.zh: 他为那设立他的尽忠，如同摩西在　神的全家尽忠一样。
3.en: who was faithful to him who appointed him, as also Moses was in all his house.

3.zh: 他比摩西算是更配多得荣耀，好像建造房屋的比房屋更尊荣；
3.en: For he has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, because he who built the house has more honor than the house.

3.zh: 因为房屋都必有人建造，但建造万物的就是　神。
3.en: For every house is built by someone; but he who built all things is God.

3.zh: 摩西为仆人，在　神的全家诚然尽忠，为要证明将来必传说的事。
3.en: Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were afterward to be spoken,

3.zh: 但基督为儿子，治理　神的家；我们若将可夸的盼望和胆量坚持到底，便是他的家了。
3.en: but Christ is faithful as a Son over his house. We are his house, if we hold fast our confidence and the glorying of our hope firm to the end.

3.zh: 圣灵有话说： 你们今日若听他的话，
3.en: Therefore, even as the Holy Spirit says, “Today if you will hear his voice,

3.zh: 就不可硬着心， 像在旷野惹他发怒、 试探他的时候一样。
3.en: don’t harden your hearts as in the rebellion, in the day of the trial in the wilderness,

3.zh: 在那里，你们的祖宗试我探我， 并且观看我的作为有四十年之久。
3.en: where your fathers tested me and tried me, and saw my deeds for forty years.

3.zh: 所以，我厌烦那世代的人，说： 他们心里常常迷糊， 竟不晓得我的作为！
3.en: Therefore I was displeased with that generation, and said, ‘They always err in their heart, but they didn’t know my ways.’

3.zh: 我就在怒中起誓说： 他们断不可进入我的安息。
3.en: As I swore in my wrath, ‘They will not enter into my rest.’”

3.zh: 弟兄们，你们要谨慎，免得你们中间或有人存着不信的恶心，把永生　神离弃了。
3.en: Beware, brothers, lest perhaps there might be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, in falling away from the living God;

3.zh: 总要趁着还有今日，天天彼此相劝，免得你们中间有人被罪迷惑，心里就刚硬了。
3.en: but exhort one another day by day, so long as it is called “today”, lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.

3.zh: 我们若将起初确实的信心坚持到底，就在基督里有分了。
3.en: For we have become partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence firm to the end,

3.zh: [经上]说：「你们今日若听他的话，就不可硬着心，像惹他发怒的日子一样。」
3.en: while it is said, “Today if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts, as in the rebellion.”

3.zh: 那时，听见他话惹他发怒的是谁呢？岂不是跟着摩西从埃及出来的众人吗？
3.en: For who, when they heard, rebelled? Wasn’t it all those who came out of Egypt led by Moses?

3.zh: 神四十年之久，又厌烦谁呢？岂不是那些犯罪、尸首倒在旷野的人吗？
3.en: With whom was he displeased forty years? Wasn’t it with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

3.zh: 又向谁起誓，不容他们进入他的安息呢？岂不是向那些不信从的人吗？
3.en: To whom did he swear that they wouldn’t enter into his rest, but to those who were disobedient?

3.zh: 这样看来，他们不能进入[安息]是因为不信的缘故了。
3.en: We see that they weren’t able to enter in because of unbelief.

4.zh: 我们既蒙留下，有进入他安息的应许，就当畏惧，免得我们中间或有人似乎是赶不上了。
4.en: Let’s fear therefore, lest perhaps anyone of you should seem to have come short of a promise of entering into his rest.

4.zh: 因为有福音传给我们，像传给他们一样；只是所听见的道与他们无益，因为他们没有信心与所听见的道调和。
4.en: For indeed we have had good news preached to us, even as they also did, but the word they heard didn’t profit them, because it wasn’t mixed with faith by those who heard.

4.zh: 但我们已经相信的人得以进入那安息，正如　神所说：「我在怒中起誓说：『他们断不可进入我的安息！』」其实造物之工，从创世以来已经成全了。
4.en: For we who have believed do enter into that rest, even as he has said, “As I swore in my wrath, they will not enter into my rest;” although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.

4.zh: 论到第七日，有一处说：「到第七日，　神就歇了他一切的工。」
4.en: For he has said this somewhere about the seventh day, “God rested on the seventh day from all his works;”

4.zh: 又有一处说：「他们断不可进入我的安息！」
4.en: and in this place again, “They will not enter into my rest.”

4.zh: 既有必进安息的人，那先前听见福音的，因为不信从，不得进去。
4.en: Seeing therefore it remains that some should enter into it, and they to whom the good news was preached before failed to enter in because of disobedience,

4.zh: 所以过了多年，就在大卫的书上，又限定一日，如以上所引的说：「你们今日若听他的话，就不可硬着心。」
4.en: he again defines a certain day, “today”, saying through David so long a time afterward (just as has been said), “Today if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts.”

4.zh: 若是约书亚已叫他们享了安息，后来　神就不再提别的日子了。
4.en: For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not have spoken afterward of another day.

4.zh: 这样看来，必另有一安息日的安息为　神的子民存留。
4.en: There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God.

4.zh: 因为那进入安息的，乃是歇了自己的工，正如　神歇了他的工一样。
4.en: For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.

4.zh: 所以，我们务必竭力进入那安息，免得有人学那不信从的样子跌倒了。
4.en: Let’s therefore give diligence to enter into that rest, lest anyone fall after the same example of disobedience.

4.zh: 神的道是活泼的，是有功效的，比一切两刃的剑更快，甚至魂与灵，骨节与骨髓，都能刺入、剖开，连心中的思念和主意都能辨明。
4.en: For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is able to discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

4.zh: 并且被造的没有一样在他面前不显然的；原来万物在那与我们有关系的主眼前，都是赤露敞开的。
4.en: There is no creature that is hidden from his sight, but all things are naked and laid open before the eyes of him to whom we must give an account.

4.zh: 我们既然有一位已经升入高天尊荣的大祭司，就是　神的儿子耶稣，便当持定所承认的道。
4.en: Having then a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let’s hold tightly to our confession.

4.zh: 因我们的大祭司并非不能体恤我们的软弱。他也曾凡事受过试探，与我们一样，只是他没有犯罪。
4.en: For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin.

4.zh: 所以，我们只管坦然无惧地来到施恩的宝座前，为要得怜恤，蒙恩惠，作随时的帮助。
4.en: Let’s therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and may find grace for help in time of need.

5.zh: 凡从人间挑选的大祭司，是奉派替人办理属　神的事，为要献上礼物和赎罪祭。
5.en: For every high priest, being taken from among men, is appointed for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.

5.zh: 他能体谅那愚蒙的和失迷的人，因为他自己也是被软弱所困。
5.en: The high priest can deal gently with those who are ignorant and going astray, because he himself is also surrounded with weakness.

5.zh: 故此，他理当为百姓和自己献祭赎罪。
5.en: Because of this, he must offer sacrifices for sins for the people, as well as for himself.

5.zh: 这[大祭司的]尊荣，没有人自取。惟要蒙　神所召，像亚伦一样。
5.en: Nobody takes this honor on himself, but he is called by God, just like Aaron was.

5.zh: 如此，基督也不是自取荣耀作大祭司，乃是在乎向他说「你是我的儿子，我今日生你」的那一位；
5.en: So also Christ didn’t glorify himself to be made a high priest, but it was he who said to him, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father.”

5.zh: 就如[经上]又有一处说：「你是照着麦基洗德的等次永远为祭司。」
5.en: As he says also in another place, “You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek.”

5.zh: 基督在肉体的时候，既大声哀哭，流泪祷告，恳求那能救他免死的主，就因他的虔诚蒙了应允。
5.en: He, in the days of his flesh, having offered up prayers and petitions with strong crying and tears to him who was able to save him from death, and having been heard for his godly fear,

5.zh: 他虽然为儿子，还是因所受的苦难学了顺从。
5.en: though he was a Son, yet learned obedience by the things which he suffered.

5.zh: 他既得以完全，就为凡顺从他的人成了永远得救的根源，
5.en: Having been made perfect, he became to all of those who obey him the author of eternal salvation,

5.zh: 并蒙　神照着麦基洗德的等次称他为大祭司。
5.en: named by God a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.

5.zh: 论到麦基洗德，我们有好些话，并且难以解明，因为你们听不进去。
5.en: About him we have many words to say, and hard to interpret, seeing you have become dull of hearing.

5.zh: 看你们学习的工夫，本该作师傅，谁知还得有人将　神圣言小学的开端另教导你们，并且成了那必须吃奶、不能吃干粮的人。
5.en: For although by this time you should be teachers, you again need to have someone teach you the rudiments of the first principles of the revelations of God. You have come to need milk, and not solid food.

5.zh: 凡只能吃奶的都不熟练仁义的道理，因为他是婴孩；
5.en: For everyone who lives on milk is not experienced in the word of righteousness, for he is a baby.

5.zh: 惟独长大成人的才能吃干粮；他们的心窍习练得通达，就能分辨好歹了。
5.en: But solid food is for those who are full grown, who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern good and evil.

6.zh: 所以，我们应当离开基督道理的开端，竭力进到完全的地步，不必再立根基，就如那懊悔死行、信靠　神、
6.en: Therefore leaving the teaching of the first principles of Christ, let’s press on to perfection—not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, of faith toward God,

6.zh: 各样洗礼、按手之礼、死人复活，以及永远审判各等教训。
6.en: of the teaching of baptisms, of laying on of hands, of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

6.zh: 神若许我们，我们必如此行。
6.en: This will we do, if God permits.

6.zh: 论到那些已经蒙了光照、尝过天恩的滋味、又于圣灵有分，
6.en: For concerning those who were once enlightened and tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit,

6.zh: 并尝过　神善道的滋味、觉悟来世权能的人，
6.en: and tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come,

6.zh: 若是离弃[道]理，就不能叫他们从新懊悔了。因为他们把　神的儿子重钉十字架，明明地羞辱他。
6.en: and then fell away, it is impossible to renew them again to repentance; seeing they crucify the Son of God for themselves again, and put him to open shame.

6.zh: 就如一块田地，吃过屡次下的雨水，生长菜蔬，合乎耕种的人用，就从　神得福；
6.en: For the land which has drunk the rain that comes often on it and produces a crop suitable for them for whose sake it is also tilled, receives blessing from God;

6.zh: 若长荆棘和蒺藜，必被废弃，近于咒诅，结局就是焚烧。
6.en: but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near being cursed, whose end is to be burned.

6.zh: 亲爱的弟兄们，我们虽是这样说，却深信你们的行为强过这些，而且近乎得救。
6.en: But, beloved, we are persuaded of better things for you, and things that accompany salvation, even though we speak like this.

6.zh: 因为　神并非不公义，竟忘记你们所做的工和你们为他名所显的爱心，就是先前伺候圣徒，如今还是伺候。
6.en: For God is not unrighteous, so as to forget your work and the labor of love which you showed toward his name, in that you served the saints, and still do serve them.

6.zh: 我们愿你们各人都显出这样的殷勤，使你们有满足的指望，一直到底。
6.en: We desire that each one of you may show the same diligence to the fullness of hope even to the end,

6.zh: 并且不懈怠，总要效法那些凭信心和忍耐承受应许的人。
6.en: that you won’t be sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and perseverance inherited the promises.

6.zh: 当初　神应许亚伯拉罕的时候，因为没有比自己更大可以指着起誓的，就指着自己起誓，说：
6.en: For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he could swear by no one greater, he swore by himself,

6.zh: 「论福，我必赐大福给你；论子孙，我必叫你的子孙多起来。」
6.en: saying, “Surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.”

6.zh: 这样，亚伯拉罕既恒久忍耐，就得了所应许的。
6.en: Thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.

6.zh: 人都是指着比自己大的起誓，并且以起誓为实据，了结各样的争论。
6.en: For men indeed swear by a greater one, and in every dispute of theirs the oath is final for confirmation.

6.zh: 照样，　神愿意为那承受应许的人格外显明他的旨意是不更改的，就起誓为证。
6.en: In this way God, being determined to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, interposed with an oath,

6.zh: 借这两件不更改的事，　神决不能说谎，好叫我们这逃往避难所、持定摆在我们前头指望的人可以大得勉励。
6.en: that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to take hold of the hope set before us.

6.zh: 我们有这指望，如同灵魂的锚，又坚固又牢靠，且通入幔内。
6.en: This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil,

6.zh: 作先锋的耶稣，既照着麦基洗德的等次成了永远的大祭司，就为我们进入幔内。
6.en: where as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.

7.zh: 这麦基洗德就是撒冷王，又是至高　神的祭司，本是长远为祭司的。他当亚伯拉罕杀败诸王回来的时候，就迎接他，给他祝福。
7.en: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,

7.zh: 亚伯拉罕也将自己所得来的，取十分之一给他。他头一个名翻出来就是仁义王，他又名撒冷王，就是平安王的意思。
7.en: to whom also Abraham divided a tenth part of all (being first, by interpretation, “king of righteousness”, and then also “king of Salem”, which means “king of peace”,

7.zh: 他无父，无母，无族谱，无生之始，无命之终，乃是与　神的儿子相似。
7.en: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like the Son of God), remains a priest continually.

7.zh: 你们想一想，先祖亚伯拉罕将自己所掳来上等之物取十分之一给他，这人是何等尊贵呢！
7.en: Now consider how great this man was, to whom even Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth out of the best plunder.

7.zh: 那得祭司职任的利未子孙，领命照例向百姓取十分之一，这百姓是自己的弟兄，虽是从亚伯拉罕身中生的，还是照例[取十分之一]。
7.en: They indeed of the sons of Levi who receive the priest’s office have a commandment to take tithes from the people according to the law, that is, of their brothers, though these have come out of the body of Abraham,

7.zh: 独有麦基洗德，不与他们同谱，倒收纳亚伯拉罕的十分之一，为那蒙应许的亚伯拉罕祝福。
7.en: but he whose genealogy is not counted from them has accepted tithes from Abraham, and has blessed him who has the promises.

7.zh: 从来位分大的给位分小的祝福，这是驳不倒的理。
7.en: But without any dispute the lesser is blessed by the greater.

7.zh: 在这里收十分之一的都是必死的人；但在那里收十分之一的，有为他作见证的说，他是活的；
7.en: Here people who die receive tithes, but there one receives tithes of whom it is testified that he lives.

7.zh: 并且可说那受十分之一的利未，也是借着亚伯拉罕纳了十分之一。
7.en: We can say that through Abraham even Levi, who receives tithes, has paid tithes,

7.zh: 因为麦基洗德迎接亚伯拉罕的时候，利未已经在他先祖的身中。
7.en: for he was yet in the body of his father when Melchizedek met him.

7.zh: 从前百姓在利未人祭司职任以下受律法，倘若借这职任能得完全，又何用另外兴起一位祭司，照麦基洗德的等次，不照亚伦的等次呢？
7.en: Now if perfection was through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people have received the law), what further need was there for another priest to arise after the order of Melchizedek, and not be called after the order of Aaron?

7.zh: 祭司的职任既已更改，律法也必须更改。
7.en: For the priesthood being changed, there is of necessity a change made also in the law.

7.zh: 因为这话所指的人本属别的支派，那支派里从来没有一人伺候祭坛。
7.en: For he of whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has officiated at the altar.

7.zh: 我们的主分明是从犹大出来的；但这支派，摩西并没有提到祭司。
7.en: For it is evident that our Lord has sprung out of Judah, about which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood.

7.zh: 倘若照麦基洗德的样式，另外兴起一位祭司来，[我的话]更是显而易见的了。
7.en: This is yet more abundantly evident, if after the likeness of Melchizedek there arises another priest,

7.zh: 他成为祭司，并不是照属肉体的条例，乃是照无穷之生命的大能。
7.en: who has been made, not after the law of a fleshly commandment, but after the power of an endless life;

7.zh: 因为有给他作见证的说：「你是照着麦基洗德的等次永远为祭司。」
7.en: for it is testified, “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”

7.zh: 先前的条例，因软弱无益，所以废掉了，
7.en: For there is an annulling of a foregoing commandment because of its weakness and uselessness

7.zh: （律法原来一无所成）就引进了更美的指望；靠这指望，我们便可以进到　神面前。
7.en: (for the law made nothing perfect), and a bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.

7.zh: 再者，[耶稣为祭司]，并不是不起誓立的。
7.en: Inasmuch as he was not made priest without the taking of an oath

7.zh: 至于那些祭司，原不是起誓立的，只有耶稣是起誓立的；因为那立他的对他说：「主起了誓，决不后悔，你是永远为祭司。」
7.en: (for they indeed have been made priests without an oath), but he with an oath by him that says of him, “The Lord swore and will not change his mind, ‘You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.’”

7.zh: 既是起誓立的，耶稣就作了更美之约的中保。
7.en: By so much, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.

7.zh: 那些成为祭司的，数目本来多，是因为有死阻隔，不能长久。
7.en: Many, indeed, have been made priests, because they are hindered from continuing by death.

7.zh: 这位既是永远常存的，他祭司的职任就长久不更换。
7.en: But he, because he lives forever, has his priesthood unchangeable.

7.zh: 凡靠着他进到　神面前的人，他都能拯救到底；因为他是长远活着，替他们祈求。
7.en: Therefore he is also able to save to the uttermost those who draw near to God through him, seeing that he lives forever to make intercession for them.

7.zh: 像这样圣洁、无邪恶、无玷污、远离罪人、高过诸天的大祭司，原是与我们合宜的。
7.en: For such a high priest was fitting for us: holy, guiltless, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;

7.zh: 他不像那些大祭司，每日必须先为自己的罪，后为百姓的罪献祭；因为他只一次将自己献上，就把这事成全了。
7.en: who doesn’t need, like those high priests, to offer up sacrifices daily, first for his own sins, and then for the sins of the people. For he did this once for all, when he offered up himself.

7.zh: 律法本是立软弱的人为大祭司；但在律法以后起誓的话，是立儿子为大祭司，乃是成全到永远的。
7.en: For the law appoints men as high priests who have weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son forever who has been perfected.

8.zh: 我们所讲的事，其中第一要紧的，就是我们有这样的大祭司，已经坐在天上至大者宝座的右边，
8.en: Now in the things which we are saying, the main point is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,

8.zh: 在圣所，就是真帐幕里，作执事；这帐幕是主所支的，不是人所支的。
8.en: a servant of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle which the Lord pitched, not man.

8.zh: 凡大祭司都是为献礼物和祭物设立的，所以这位大祭司也必须有所献的。
8.en: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices. Therefore it is necessary that this high priest also have something to offer.

8.zh: 他若在地上，必不得为祭司，因为已经有照律法献礼物的[祭司]。
8.en: For if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, seeing there are priests who offer the gifts according to the law,

8.zh: 他们供奉的事本是天上事的形状和影像，正如摩西将要造帐幕的时候，蒙　[神]警戒他，说：「你要谨慎，作各样的物件都要照着在山上指示你的样式。」
8.en: who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, even as Moses was warned by God when he was about to make the tabernacle, for he said, “See, you shall make everything according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.”

8.zh: 如今耶稣所得的职任是更美的，正如他作更美之约的中保；这约原是凭更美之应许立的。
8.en: But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as he is also the mediator of a better covenant, which on better promises has been given as law.

8.zh: 那前约若没有瑕疵，就无处寻求后约了。
8.en: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then no place would have been sought for a second.

8.zh: 所以主指责他的百姓说： 日子将到， 我要与以色列家和犹大家另立新约，
8.en: For finding fault with them, he said, “Behold, the days are coming”, says the Lord, “that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah;

8.zh: 不像我拉着他们祖宗的手， 领他们出埃及的时候， 与他们所立的约。 因为他们不恒心守我的约， 我也不理他们。 这是主说的。
8.en: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; for they didn’t continue in my covenant, and I disregarded them,” says the Lord.

8.zh: 主又说： 那些日子以后， 我与以色列家所立的约乃是这样： 我要将我的律法放在他们里面， 写在他们心上； 我要作他们的　神； 他们要作我的子民。
8.en: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days,” says the Lord: “I will put my laws into their mind; I will also write them on their heart. I will be their God, and they will be my people.

8.zh: 他们不用各人教导自己的乡邻和自己的弟兄， 说：你该认识主； 因为他们从最小的到至大的，都必认识我。
8.en: They will not teach every man his fellow citizen and every man his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for all will know me, from their least to their greatest.

8.zh: 我要宽恕他们的不义， 不再记念他们的罪愆。
8.en: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness. I will remember their sins and lawless deeds no more.”

8.zh: 既说新约，就以前约为旧了；但那渐旧渐衰的，就必快归无有了。
8.en: In that he says, “A new covenant”, he has made the first obsolete. But that which is becoming obsolete and grows aged is near to vanishing away.

9.zh: 原来前约有礼拜的条例和属世界的圣幕。
9.en: Now indeed even the first covenant had ordinances of divine service and an earthly sanctuary.

9.zh: 因为有预备的帐幕，头一层叫作圣所，里面有灯台、桌子，和陈设饼。
9.en: For a tabernacle was prepared. In the first part were the lamp stand, the table, and the show bread, which is called the Holy Place.

9.zh: 第二幔子后又有一层帐幕，叫作至圣所，
9.en: After the second veil was the tabernacle which is called the Holy of Holies,

9.zh: 有金香炉，有包金的约柜，柜里有盛吗哪的金罐和亚伦发过芽的杖，并两块约版；
9.en: having a golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant overlaid on all sides with gold, in which was a golden pot holding the manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tablets of the covenant;

9.zh: 柜上面有荣耀基路伯的影罩着施恩座。这几件我现在不能一一细说。
9.en: and above it cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, of which things we can’t speak now in detail.

9.zh: 这些物件既如此预备齐了，众祭司就常进头一层帐幕，行拜　神的礼。
9.en: Now these things having been thus prepared, the priests go in continually into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the services,

9.zh: 至于第二层帐幕，惟有大祭司一年一次独自进去，没有不带着血为自己和百姓的过错献上。
9.en: but into the second the high priest alone, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the errors of the people.

9.zh: 圣灵用此指明，头一层帐幕仍存的时候，进入至圣所的路还未显明。
9.en: The Holy Spirit is indicating this, that the way into the Holy Place wasn’t yet revealed while the first tabernacle was still standing.

9.zh: 那头一层帐幕作现今的一个表样，所献的礼物和祭物，就着良心说，都不能叫礼拜的人得以完全。
9.en: This is a symbol of the present age, where gifts and sacrifices are offered that are incapable, concerning the conscience, of making the worshiper perfect,

9.zh: 这些事，连那饮食和诸般洗濯的规矩，都不过是属肉体的条例，命定到振兴的时候为止。
9.en: being only (with foods and drinks and various washings) fleshly ordinances, imposed until a time of reformation.

9.zh: 但现在基督已经来到，作了将来美事的大祭司，经过那更大更全备的帐幕，不是人手所造，也不是属乎这世界的；
9.en: But Christ having come as a high priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this creation,

9.zh: 并且不用山羊和牛犊的血，乃用自己的血，只一次进入圣所，成了永远赎罪的事。
9.en: nor yet through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption.

9.zh: 若山羊和公牛的血，并母牛犊的灰，洒在不洁的人身上，尚且叫人成圣，身体洁净，
9.en: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify to the cleanness of the flesh,

9.zh: 何况基督借着永远的灵，将自己无瑕无疵献给　神，他的血岂不更能洗净你们的心，除去你们的死行，使你们事奉那永生　神吗？
9.en: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?

9.zh: 为此，他作了新约的中保，既然受死赎了人在前约之时所犯的罪过，便叫蒙召之人得着所应许永远的产业。
9.en: For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, since a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first covenant, that those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.

9.zh: 凡有遗命必须等到留遗命的人死了；
9.en: For where a last will and testament is, there must of necessity be the death of him who made it.

9.zh: 因为人死了，遗命才有效力，若留遗命的尚在，那遗命还有用处吗？
9.en: For a will is in force where there has been death, for it is never in force while he who made it lives.

9.zh: 所以，前约也不是不用血立的；
9.en: Therefore even the first covenant has not been dedicated without blood.

9.zh: 因为摩西当日照着律法将各样诫命传给众百姓，就拿朱红色绒和牛膝草，把牛犊山羊的血和水洒在书上，又洒在众百姓身上，说：
9.en: For when every commandment had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,

9.zh: 「这血就是　神与你们立约[的凭据]。」
9.en: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you.”

9.zh: 他又照样把血洒在帐幕和各样器皿上。
9.en: He sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry in the same way with the blood.

9.zh: 按着律法，凡物差不多都是用血洁净的；若不流血，罪就不得赦免了。
9.en: According to the law, nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and apart from shedding of blood there is no remission.

9.zh: 照着天上样式做的物件必须用这些祭物去洁净；但那天上的本物自然当用更美的祭物去洁净。
9.en: It was necessary therefore that the copies of the things in the heavens should be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

9.zh: 因为基督并不是进了人手所造的圣所（这不过是真圣所的影相），乃是进了天堂，如今为我们显在　神面前；
9.en: For Christ hasn’t entered into holy places made with hands, which are representations of the true, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us;

9.zh: 也不是多次将自己献上，像那大祭司每年带着牛羊的血进入圣所，
9.en: nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters into the holy place year by year with blood not his own,

9.zh: 如果这样，他从创世以来，就必多次受苦了。但如今在这末世显现一次，把自己献为祭，好除掉罪。
9.en: or else he must have suffered often since the foundation of the world. But now once at the end of the ages, he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.

9.zh: 按着定命，人人都有一死，死后且有审判。
9.en: Inasmuch as it is appointed for men to die once, and after this, judgment,

9.zh: 像这样，基督既然一次被献，担当了多人的罪，将来要向那等候他的人第二次显现，并与罪无关，乃是为拯救他们。
9.en: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to save those who are eagerly waiting for him.

10.zh: 律法既是将来美事的影儿，不是本物的真像，总不能借着每年常献一样的祭物叫那近前来的人得以完全。
10.en: For the law, having a shadow of the good to come, not the very image of the things, can never with the same sacrifices year by year, which they offer continually, make perfect those who draw near.

10.zh: 若不然，献祭的事岂不早已止住了吗？因为礼拜的人，良心既被洁净，就不再觉得有罪了。
10.en: Or else wouldn’t they have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, having been once cleansed, would have had no more consciousness of sins?

10.zh: 但这些[祭物]是叫人每年想起罪来；
10.en: But in those sacrifices there is a yearly reminder of sins.

10.zh: 因为公牛和山羊的血，断不能除罪。
10.en: For it is impossible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.

10.zh: 所以基督到世上来的时候，就说： 　[神啊]，祭物和礼物是你不愿意的； 你曾给我预备了身体。
10.en: Therefore when he comes into the world, he says, “You didn’t desire sacrifice and offering, but you prepared a body for me.

10.zh: 燔祭和赎罪[祭]是你不喜欢的。
10.en: You had no pleasure in whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin.

10.zh: 那时我说：　神啊，我来了， 为要照你的旨意行； 我的事在经卷上已经记载了。
10.en: Then I said, ‘Behold, I have come (in the scroll of the book it is written of me) to do your will, O God.’”

10.zh: 以上说：「祭物和礼物，燔祭和赎罪祭，是你不愿意的，也是你不喜欢的（这都是按着律法献的）」；
10.en: Previously saying, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin you didn’t desire, neither had pleasure in them” (those which are offered according to the law),

10.zh: 后又说：「我来了为要照你的旨意行」；[可见]他是除去在先的，为要立定在后的。
10.en: then he has said, “Behold, I have come to do your will.” He takes away the first, that he may establish the second,

10.zh: 我们凭这旨意，靠耶稣基督，只一次献上他的身体，就得以成圣。
10.en: by which will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

10.zh: 凡祭司天天站着事奉　[神]，屡次献上一样的祭物，这祭物永不能除罪。
10.en: Every priest indeed stands day by day serving and offering often the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins,

10.zh: 但基督献了一次永远的赎罪祭，就在　神的右边坐下了。
10.en: but he, when he had offered one sacrifice for sins forever, sat down on the right hand of God,

10.zh: 从此，等候他仇敌成了他的脚凳。
10.en: from that time waiting until his enemies are made the footstool of his feet.

10.zh: 因为他一次献祭，便叫那得以成圣的人永远完全。
10.en: For by one offering he has perfected forever those who are being sanctified.

10.zh: 圣灵也对我们作见证；因为他既已说过：
10.en: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after saying,

10.zh: 主说：那些日子以后， 我与他们所立的约乃是这样： 我要将我的律法写在他们心上， 又要放在他们的里面。
10.en: “This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days,” says the Lord, “I will put my laws on their heart, I will also write them on their mind;” then he says,

10.zh: [以后就说]： 我不再记念他们的罪愆和他们的过犯。
10.en: “I will remember their sins and their iniquities no more.”

10.zh: 这些罪过既已赦免，就不用再为罪献祭了。
10.en: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.

10.zh: 弟兄们，我们既因耶稣的血得以坦然进入至圣所，
10.en: Having therefore, brothers, boldness to enter into the holy place by the blood of Jesus,

10.zh: 是借着他给我们开了一条又新又活的路，从幔子经过，这幔子就是他的身体。
10.en: by the way which he dedicated for us, a new and living way, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh,

10.zh: 又有一位大祭司治理　神的家，
10.en: and having a great priest over God’s house,

10.zh: 并我们心中天良的亏欠已经洒去，身体用清水洗净了，就当存着诚心和充足的信心来到　神面前；
10.en: let’s draw near with a true heart in fullness of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and having our body washed with pure water,

10.zh: 也要坚守我们所承认的指望，不至摇动，因为那应许我们的是信实的。
10.en: let’s hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering; for he who promised is faithful.

10.zh: 又要彼此相顾，激发爱心，勉励行善。
10.en: Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,

10.zh: 你们不可停止聚会，好像那些停止惯了的人，倒要彼此劝勉，既知道那日子临近，就更当如此。
10.en: not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

10.zh: 因为我们得知真道以后，若故意犯罪，赎罪的祭就再没有了；
10.en: For if we sin willfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more a sacrifice for sins,

10.zh: 惟有战惧等候审判和那烧灭众敌人的烈火。
10.en: but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and a fierceness of fire which will devour the adversaries.

10.zh: 人干犯摩西的律法，凭两三个见证人，尚且不得怜恤而死，
10.en: A man who disregards Moses’ law dies without compassion on the word of two or three witnesses.

10.zh: 何况人践踏　神的儿子，将那使他成圣之约的血当作平常，又亵慢施恩的[圣]灵，你们想，他要受的刑罚该怎样加重呢！
10.en: How much worse punishment do you think he will be judged worthy of who has trodden under foot the Son of God, and has counted the blood of the covenant with which he was sanctified an unholy thing, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?

10.zh: 因为我们知道谁说：「伸冤在我，我必报应」；又[说]：「主要审判他的百姓。」
10.en: For we know him who said, “Vengeance belongs to me. I will repay,” says the Lord. Again, “The Lord will judge his people.”

10.zh: 落在永生　神的手里，真是可怕的！
10.en: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

10.zh: 你们要追念往日，蒙了光照以后所忍受大争战的各样苦难：
10.en: But remember the former days, in which, after you were enlightened, you endured a great struggle with sufferings:

10.zh: 一面被毁谤，遭患难，成了戏景，叫众人观看；一面陪伴那些受这样苦难的人。
10.en: partly, being exposed to both reproaches and oppressions, and partly, becoming partakers with those who were treated so.

10.zh: 因为你们体恤了那些被捆锁的人，并且你们的家业被人抢去，也甘心忍受，知道自己有更美长存的家业。
10.en: For you both had compassion on me in my chains and joyfully accepted the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you have for yourselves a better possession and an enduring one in the heavens.

10.zh: 所以，你们不可丢弃勇敢的心；存这样的心必得大赏赐。
10.en: Therefore don’t throw away your boldness, which has a great reward.

10.zh: 你们必须忍耐，使你们行完了　神的旨意，就可以得着所应许的。
10.en: For you need endurance so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.

10.zh: 因为还有一点点时候， 那要来的就来，并不迟延；
10.en: “In a very little while, he who comes will come and will not wait.

10.zh: 只是义人必因信得生。 他若退后，我心里就不喜欢他。
10.en: But the righteous one will live by faith. If he shrinks back, my soul has no pleasure in him.”

10.zh: 我们却不是退后入沉沦的那等人，乃是有信心以致灵魂得救的人。
10.en: But we are not of those who shrink back to destruction, but of those who have faith to the saving of the soul.

11.zh: 信就是所望之事的实底，是未见之事的确据。
11.en: Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.

11.zh: 古人在这信上得了美好的证据。
11.en: For by this, the elders obtained approval.

11.zh: 我们因着信，就知道诸世界是借　神的话造成的；这样，所看见的，并不是从显然之物造出来的。
11.en: By faith we understand that the universe has been framed by the word of God, so that what is seen has not been made out of things which are visible.

11.zh: 亚伯因着信，献祭与　神，比该隐所献的更美，因此便得了称义的见证，就是　神指他礼物作的见证。他虽然死了，却因这信，仍旧说话。
11.en: By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he had testimony given to him that he was righteous, God testifying with respect to his gifts; and through it he, being dead, still speaks.

11.zh: 以诺因着信，被接去，不至于见死，人也找不着他，因为　神已经把他接去了；只是他被接去以先，已经得了　神喜悦他的明证。
11.en: By faith Enoch was taken away, so that he wouldn’t see death, and he was not found, because God translated him. For he has had testimony given to him that before his translation he had been well pleasing to God.

11.zh: 人非有信，就不能得　神的喜悦；因为到　神面前来的人必须信有　神，且信他赏赐那寻求他的人。
11.en: Without faith it is impossible to be well pleasing to him, for he who comes to God must believe that he exists, and that he is a rewarder of those who seek him.

11.zh: 挪亚因着信，既蒙　[神]指示他未见的事，动了敬畏的心，预备了一只方舟，使他全家得救。因此就定了那世代的罪，自己也承受了那从信而来的义。
11.en: By faith Noah, being warned about things not yet seen, moved with godly fear, prepared a ship for the saving of his house, through which he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness which is according to faith.

11.zh: 亚伯拉罕因着信，蒙召的时候就遵命出去，往将来要得为业的地方去；出去的时候，还不知往哪里去。
11.en: By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to the place which he was to receive for an inheritance. He went out, not knowing where he went.

11.zh: 他因着信，就在所应许之地作客，好像在异地居住帐棚，与那同蒙一个应许的以撒、雅各一样。
11.en: By faith he lived as an alien in the land of promise, as in a land not his own, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise.

11.zh: 因为他等候那座有根基的城，就是　神所经营所建造的。
11.en: For he was looking for the city which has foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

11.zh: 因着信，连撒拉自己，虽然过了生育的岁数，还能怀孕，因她以为那应许她的是可信的。
11.en: By faith even Sarah herself received power to conceive, and she bore a child when she was past age, since she counted him faithful who had promised.

11.zh: 所以从一个仿佛已死的人就生出[子孙]，如同天上的星那样众多，海边的沙那样无数。
11.en: Therefore as many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as innumerable as the sand which is by the sea shore, were fathered by one man, and him as good as dead.

11.zh: 这些人都是存着信心死的，并没有得着所应许的；却从远处望见，且欢喜迎接，又承认自己在世上是客旅，是寄居的。
11.en: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them and embraced them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

11.zh: 说这样话的人是表明自己要找一个家乡。
11.en: For those who say such things make it clear that they are seeking a country of their own.

11.zh: 他们若想念所离开的家乡，还有可以回去的机会。
11.en: If indeed they had been thinking of that country from which they went out, they would have had enough time to return.

11.zh: 他们却羡慕一个更美的家乡，就是在天上的。所以　神被称为他们的　神，并不以为耻，因为他已经给他们预备了一座城。
11.en: But now they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.

11.zh: 亚伯拉罕因着信，被试验的时候，就把以撒献上；这便是那欢喜领受应许的，将自己独生的儿子献上。
11.en: By faith, Abraham, being tested, offered up Isaac. Yes, he who had gladly received the promises was offering up his only born son,

11.zh: [论到这儿子]，曾有话说：「从以撒生的才要称为你的后裔。」
11.en: to whom it was said, “Your offspring will be accounted as from Isaac,”

11.zh: 他以为　神还能叫人从死里复活；他也仿佛从死中得回他的儿子来。
11.en: concluding that God is able to raise up even from the dead. Figuratively speaking, he also did receive him back from the dead.

11.zh: 以撒因着信，就指着将来的事给雅各、以扫祝福。
11.en: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.

11.zh: 雅各因着信，临死的时候，给约瑟的两个儿子各自祝福，扶着杖头敬拜　神。
11.en: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.

11.zh: 约瑟因着信，临终的时候，提到以色列族将来要出[埃及]，并为自己的骸骨留下遗命。
11.en: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, made mention of the departure of the children of Israel, and gave instructions concerning his bones.

11.zh: 摩西生下来，他的父母见他是个俊美的孩子，就因着信，把他藏了三个月，并不怕王命。
11.en: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that he was a beautiful child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.

11.zh: 摩西因着信，长大了就不肯称为法老女儿之子。
11.en: By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter,

11.zh: 他宁可和　神的百姓同受苦害，也不愿暂时享受罪中之乐。
11.en: choosing rather to share ill treatment with God’s people than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a time,

11.zh: 他看为基督受的凌辱比埃及的财物更宝贵，因他想望所要得的赏赐。
11.en: considering the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt; for he looked to the reward.

11.zh: 他因着信，就离开埃及，不怕王怒；因为他恒心忍耐，如同看见那不能看见的[主]。
11.en: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.

11.zh: 他因着信，就守逾越节，行洒血的礼，免得那灭长子的临近以色列人。
11.en: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, that the destroyer of the firstborn should not touch them.

11.zh: 他们因着信，过红海如行干地；埃及人试着要过去，就被吞灭了。
11.en: By faith they passed through the Red Sea as on dry land. When the Egyptians tried to do so, they were swallowed up.

11.zh: 以色列人因着信，围绕耶利哥城七日，城墙就倒塌了。
11.en: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down after they had been encircled for seven days.

11.zh: 妓女喇合因着信，曾和和平平地接待探子，就不与那些不顺从的人一同灭亡。
11.en: By faith Rahab the prostitute didn’t perish with those who were disobedient, having received the spies in peace.

11.zh: 我又何必再说呢？若要一一细说，基甸、巴拉、参孙、耶弗他、大卫、撒母耳，和众先知的事，时候就不够了。
11.en: What more shall I say? For the time would fail me if I told of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets—

11.zh: 他们因着信，制伏了敌国，行了公义，得了应许，堵了狮子的口，
11.en: who through faith subdued kingdoms, worked out righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,

11.zh: 灭了烈火的猛势，脱了刀剑的锋刃；软弱变为刚强，争战显出勇敢，打退外邦的全军。
11.en: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, from weakness were made strong, grew mighty in war, and caused foreign armies to flee.

11.zh: 有妇人得自己的死人复活。又有人忍受严刑，不肯苟且得释放，为要得着更美的复活。
11.en: Women received their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured, not accepting their deliverance, that they might obtain a better resurrection.

11.zh: 又有人忍受戏弄、鞭打、捆锁、监禁、各等的磨炼，
11.en: Others were tried by mocking and scourging, yes, moreover by bonds and imprisonment.

11.zh: 被石头打死，被锯锯死，受试探，被刀杀，披着绵羊山羊的皮各处奔跑，受穷乏、患难、苦害，
11.en: They were stoned. They were sawn apart. They were tempted. They were slain with the sword. They went around in sheep skins and in goat skins; being destitute, afflicted, ill-treated—

11.zh: 在旷野、山岭、山洞、地穴，飘流无定，本是世界不配有的人。
11.en: of whom the world was not worthy—wandering in deserts, mountains, caves, and the holes of the earth.

11.zh: 这些人都是因信得了美好的证据，却仍未得着所应许的；
11.en: These all, having been commended for their faith, didn’t receive the promise,

11.zh: 因为　神给我们预备了更美的事，叫他们若不与我们同得，就不能完全。
11.en: God having provided some better thing concerning us, so that apart from us they should not be made perfect.

12.zh: 我们既有这许多的见证人，如同云彩围着我们，就当放下各样的重担，脱去容易缠累我们的罪，存心忍耐，奔那摆在我们前头的路程，
12.en: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,

12.zh: 仰望为我们信心创始成终的耶稣。他因那摆在前面的喜乐，就轻看羞辱，忍受了十字架[的苦难]，便坐在　神宝座的右边。
12.en: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

12.zh: 那忍受罪人这样顶撞的，你们要思想，免得疲倦灰心。
12.en: For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.

12.zh: 你们与罪恶相争，还没有抵挡到流血的地步。
12.en: You have not yet resisted to blood, striving against sin.

12.zh: 你们又忘了那劝你们如同劝儿子的话，说： 我儿，你不可轻看主的管教， 被他责备的时候也不可灰心；
12.en: You have forgotten the exhortation which reasons with you as with children, “My son, don’t take lightly the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when you are reproved by him;

12.zh: 因为主所爱的，他必管教， 又鞭打凡所收纳的儿子。
12.en: for whom the Lord loves, he disciplines, and chastises every son whom he receives.”

12.zh: 你们所忍受的，是　神管教你们，待你们如同待儿子。焉有儿子不被父亲管教的呢？
12.en: It is for discipline that you endure. God deals with you as with children, for what son is there whom his father doesn’t discipline?

12.zh: 管教原是众子所共受的。你们若不受管教，就是私子，不是儿子了。
12.en: But if you are without discipline, of which all have been made partakers, then you are illegitimate, and not children.

12.zh: 再者，我们曾有生身的父管教我们，我们尚且敬重他，何况万灵的父，我们岂不更当顺服他得生吗？
12.en: Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh to chasten us, and we paid them respect. Shall we not much rather be in subjection to the Father of spirits and live?

12.zh: 生身的父都是暂随己意管教我们；惟有万灵的父管教我们，是要我们得益处，使我们在他的圣洁上有分。
12.en: For they indeed for a few days disciplined us as seemed good to them, but he for our profit, that we may be partakers of his holiness.

12.zh: 凡管教的事，当时不觉得快乐，反觉得愁苦；后来却为那经练过的人结出平安的果子，就是义。
12.en: All chastening seems for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.

12.zh: 所以，你们要把下垂的手、发酸的腿挺起来；
12.en: Therefore lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees,

12.zh: 也要为自己的脚，把道路修直了，使瘸子不致歪脚，反得痊愈。
12.en: and make straight paths for your feet, so what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather be healed.

12.zh: 你们要追求与众人和睦，并要追求圣洁；非圣洁没有人能见主。
12.en: Follow after peace with all men, and the sanctification without which no man will see the Lord,

12.zh: 又要谨慎，恐怕有人失了　神的恩；恐怕有毒根生出来扰乱你们，因此叫众人沾染污秽；
12.en: looking carefully lest there be any man who falls short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you and many be defiled by it,

12.zh: 恐怕有淫乱的，有贪恋世俗如以扫的，他因一点食物把自己长子的名分卖了。
12.en: lest there be any sexually immoral person or profane person, like Esau, who sold his birthright for one meal.

12.zh: 后来想要承受父所祝的福，竟被弃绝，虽然号哭切求，却得不着门路使他[父亲]的心意回转。这是你们知道的。
12.en: For you know that even when he afterward desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for a change of mind though he sought it diligently with tears.

12.zh: 你们原不是来到那能摸的山；此山有火焰、密云、黑暗、暴风、
12.en: For you have not come to a mountain that might be touched and that burned with fire, and to blackness, darkness, storm,

12.zh: 角声与说话的声音。那些听见这声音的，都求不要再向他们说话；
12.en: the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which those who heard it begged that not one more word should be spoken to them,

12.zh: 因为他们当不起所命他们的话，说：「靠近这山的，即便是走兽，也要用石头打死。」
12.en: for they could not stand that which was commanded, “If even an animal touches the mountain, it shall be stoned”.

12.zh: 所见的极其可怕，甚至摩西说：「我甚是恐惧战兢。」
12.en: So fearful was the appearance that Moses said, “I am terrified and trembling.”

12.zh: 你们乃是来到锡安山，永生　神的城邑，就是天上的耶路撒冷。那里有千万的天使，
12.en: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable multitudes of angels,

12.zh: 有名录在天上诸长子之会所共聚的总会，有审判众人的　神和被成全之义人的灵魂，
12.en: to the festal gathering and assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of just men made perfect,

12.zh: 并新约的中保耶稣，以及所洒的血；这血所说的比亚伯的血所说的更美。
12.en: to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better than that of Abel.

12.zh: 你们总要谨慎，不可弃绝那向你们说话的。因为，那些弃绝在地上警戒他们的尚且不能逃罪，何况我们违背那从天上警戒我们的呢？
12.en: See that you don’t refuse him who speaks. For if they didn’t escape when they refused him who warned on the earth, how much more will we not escape who turn away from him who warns from heaven,

12.zh: 当时他的声音震动了地，但如今他应许说：「再一次我不单要震动地，还要震动天。」
12.en: whose voice shook the earth then, but now he has promised, saying, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heavens.”

12.zh: 这再一次的话，是指明被震动的，就是受造之物都要挪去，使那不被震动的常存。
12.en: This phrase, “Yet once more” signifies the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that have been made, that those things which are not shaken may remain.

12.zh: 所以我们既得了不能震动的国，就当感恩，照　神所喜悦的，用虔诚、敬畏的心事奉　神。
12.en: Therefore, receiving a Kingdom that can’t be shaken, let’s have grace, through which we serve God acceptably, with reverence and awe,

12.zh: 因为我们的　神乃是烈火。
12.en: for our God is a consuming fire.

13.zh: 你们务要常存弟兄相爱的心。
13.en: Let brotherly love continue.

13.zh: 不可忘记用爱心接待客旅；因为曾有接待客旅的，不知不觉就接待了天使。
13.en: Don’t forget to show hospitality to strangers, for in doing so, some have entertained angels without knowing it.

13.zh: 你们要记念被捆绑的人，好像与他们同受捆绑；也要记念遭苦害的人，想到自己也在肉身之内。
13.en: Remember those who are in bonds, as bound with them, and those who are ill-treated, since you are also in the body.

13.zh: 婚姻，人人都当尊重，床也不可污秽；因为苟合行淫的人，　神必要审判。
13.en: Let marriage be held in honor among all, and let the bed be undefiled; but God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.

13.zh: 你们存心不可贪爱钱财，要以自己所有的为足；因为主曾说：「我总不撇下你，也不丢弃你。」
13.en: Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have, for he has said, “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.”

13.zh: 所以我们可以放胆说： 主是帮助我的，我必不惧怕； 人能把我怎么样呢？
13.en: So that with good courage we say, “The Lord is my helper. I will not fear. What can man do to me?”

13.zh: 从前引导你们、传　神之道给你们的人，你们要想念他们，效法他们的信心，留心看他们为人的结局。
13.en: Remember your leaders, men who spoke to you the word of God, and considering the results of their conduct, imitate their faith.

13.zh: 耶稣基督昨日、今日、一直到永远，是一样的。
13.en: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

13.zh: 你们不要被那诸般怪异的教训勾引了去；因为人心靠恩得坚固才是好的，并不是靠饮食。那在饮食上专心的从来没有得着益处。
13.en: Don’t be carried away by various and strange teachings, for it is good that the heart be established by grace, not by foods, through which those who were so occupied were not benefited.

13.zh: 我们有一祭坛，上面的祭物是那些在帐幕中供职的人不可同吃的。
13.en: We have an altar from which those who serve the holy tabernacle have no right to eat.

13.zh: 原来牲畜的血被大祭司带入圣所作赎罪祭；牲畜的身子被烧在营外。
13.en: For the bodies of those animals, whose blood is brought into the holy place by the high priest as an offering for sin, are burned outside of the camp.

13.zh: 所以，耶稣要用自己的血叫百姓成圣，也就在城门外受苦。
13.en: Therefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people through his own blood, suffered outside of the gate.

13.zh: 这样，我们也当出到营外，就了他去，忍受他所受的凌辱。
13.en: Let’s therefore go out to him outside of the camp, bearing his reproach.

13.zh: 我们在这里本没有常存的城，乃是寻求那将来的城。
13.en: For we don’t have here an enduring city, but we seek that which is to come.

13.zh: 我们应当靠着耶稣，常常以颂赞为祭献给　神，这就是那承认主名之人嘴唇的果子。
13.en: Through him, then, let’s offer up a sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of lips which proclaim allegiance to his name.

13.zh: 只是不可忘记行善和捐输的事，因为这样的祭是　神所喜悦的。
13.en: But don’t forget to be doing good and sharing, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

13.zh: 你们要依从那些引导你们的，且要顺服；因他们为你们的灵魂时刻警醒，好像那将来交帐的人。你们要使他们交的时候有快乐，不致忧愁；若忧愁就与你们无益了。
13.en: Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they watch on behalf of your souls, as those who will give account, that they may do this with joy and not with groaning, for that would be unprofitable for you.

13.zh: 请你们为我们祷告，因我们自觉良心无亏，愿意凡事按正道而行。
13.en: Pray for us, for we are persuaded that we have a good conscience, desiring to live honorably in all things.

13.zh: 我更求你们为我祷告，使我快些回到你们那里去。
13.en: I strongly urge you to do this, that I may be restored to you sooner.

13.zh: 但愿赐平安的　神，就是那凭永约之血、使群羊的大牧人—我主耶稣从死里复活的　神，
13.en: Now may the God of peace, who brought again from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep with the blood of an eternal covenant, our Lord Jesus,

13.zh: 在各样善事上成全你们，叫你们遵行他的旨意；又借着耶稣基督在你们心里行他所喜悦的事。愿荣耀归给他，直到永永远远。阿们！
13.en: make you complete in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is well pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.

13.zh: 弟兄们，我略略写信给你们，望你们听我劝勉的话。
13.en: But I exhort you, brothers, endure the word of exhortation, for I have written to you in few words.

13.zh: 你们该知道，我们的兄弟提摩太已经释放了；他若快来，我必同他去见你们。
13.en: Know that our brother Timothy has been freed, with whom, if he comes shortly, I will see you.

13.zh: 请你们问引导你们的诸位和众圣徒安。从意大利来的人也问你们安。
13.en: Greet all of your leaders and all the saints. The Italians greet you.

13.zh: 愿恩惠[常]与你们众人同在。阿们！
13.en: Grace be with you all. Amen.
